Question
========
You've already created a histogram and now want to add a kernel density curve on top of it, in the same figure. What
happens if you call `plot()` on the density estimate to try to add it?

Answerlist
----------
* The density curve is drawn on top of the existing histogram, combining both into a single figure.
* The `plot()` call opens a brand new figure, replacing the histogram instead of adding to it.
* Nothing happens, since `plot()` cannot accept a density object as an argument.
* R throws an error and stops execution.

Solution
========

Answerlist
----------
* Wrong: `plot()` starts a new plot rather than drawing on top of an existing one.
* Correct: `plot()` always draws a fresh figure; to add a layer to an existing plot, a dedicated layering function like `lines()` is needed instead.
* Wrong: `plot()` can accept a density object; it just doesn't layer it onto an existing figure.
* Wrong: this doesn't produce an error; it silently replaces the existing plot with a new one.
